label: digit 0 input at original positions 3-6
explanation: Fires exactly when the input token is the digit 0 during the original (pre-delimiter) phase at positions 3, 4, 5 or 6. Dev precision and recall are both 1.0. It is silent on 0 at positions 0-2 and 7-8, on every other token, and on the delimiter and copy phases (including when 0 is fed back during copying). Magnitude depends on position: mean activation per firing at t=4 and t=5 is about twice that at t=3 or t=6, and the top examples are all at t=4. It still fires on repeated 0s, but on fewer of them (in_first lift is 1.6x). The firing rate goes up with the number of digits in the sequence, because more digits means more 0s.

issues: Main predicate holds up on test: precision 0.99994, recall 1.0, F1 0.99997, mass recall 1.0. There are 0 missed activations and only 3 false positives, all at t=6 on a 0 in a sequence that also has a g/j pattern. That is scattered noise, not a pattern.

Minor factual error: the claim that it 'still fires on repeated 0s, but less often than on first occurrences' is misleading. Scoring the predicate restricted to repeated 0s (n_seen([tok('0')]) > 0) gives precision 1.0 on test, so it fires on every repeated 0 at t=3-6. The in_first lift of 1.6x is measured over all tokens, not just 0s, so it is a base-rate artifact.
Magnitude claim confirmed from the dev profile: mean activation per firing (mass share / count) is about 2x higher at t=4 and t=5 than at t=3 and t=6, and the top examples are all at t=4.

The claims about phase and position are confirmed: no firing at the delimiter or in the copy phase, none at t=0-2 or t>=7, and an even rate of about 0.033 (roughly 1/30, i.e. essentially every 0) at original positions 3-6.
